decision_record.calculation: Fixture: tranche-1 fills qty 1 of full 3 -> plan {tranche2_qty: 2, signal_date: entry session, full_qty: 3}; next pass with the 5/20 turn confirmed emits the tranche-2 entry qty 2. Feed OFF at entry -> no plan file, no tranche 2, exactly pre-change.
decision_record.comparison: Pre-change live path: tranche 2 keys off pos[tranche2_qty]/pos[signal_date] — fields NO desk component writes (the journal position record carries a fixed field list without them; the adapter translates only qty/entry_px/entry_date/intent_id). Measured: on desk-originated positions tranche 2 could never fire.
decision_record.experiment: Two-pass adapters3 drive sharing one state dir (entry pass + held-position pass with turn confirmed): ON fires tranche 2; OFF-at-entry never does. Paired records appended to capitulation_enh2_paired.jsonl beside the journal on every serve.
decision_record.mechanism: Input starvation cured at the source: the v2 adapter records the tranche plan when it translates a tranche-1 entry (the intent reason states the full size verbatim, 'tranche1 (of full N)') into a state file beside the sleeve journal (the bb_rsi_divergence adapter's recorded-entry-plan pattern), and serves it merged into the position until held qty reaches the full size. The pinned sleeve's frozen tranche-2 rule then runs as designed.
decision_record.transfer: The SixSigma scale-in is the strategy: half on the capitulation signal, half on the 5/20 turn confirmation. The second half is where the confirmed reversal pays; without it every position is half-sized forever.

switch: extra.capitulation_improve.tranche_plan_feed (adapter) default ON; OFF serves the pre-change starved record exactly
